correctness.rationale: Two coordinates of a zero-sum vector are x and -x. For three, sign and permutation give (a,b,-a-b), hence 4 G² = 3 L² + (a-b)². The endpoint shapes attain both bounds, so the strict ratio cutoff follows, with equality excluded. The prescribed values are admissible index values 0 < L_A < L_B < 1; positivity at those exact values follows by taking votes v=d^-+((1-L)/3)1 and seats s=d^++((1-L)/3)1, not by rescaling a fixed prescribed L. On the grid the analogous one-unit lower bound is equivalent to integer positive discrepancy mass l ≤ N−3, by placing an integer slack vector with each entry at least one beneath both the positive and negative parts. Thus through N=10 the largest possible ratio is at most 6/7. At N=11 only l_A=7, l_B=8 can reverse. At l=7 the four possible squared Gallagher numerators are 37,39,43,49, and at l=8 the minimum is 48 with the next value 49. Exactly the two extremal shapes therefore reverse; each has six labeled versions and the l-values distinguish the members, giving 36 unordered pairs. The realizable-vector count is 1+sum_{l=1}^8 6l=217 (hexagonal shells). Independent replay python3 /workspace/reproductions/3.py confirms all layers. 'Shapes' means relabeling and sign change separately for the two elections, as in the frozen canonicalization, not a claim of one simultaneous symmetry orbit; the replay finds three simultaneous orbits of size 12. Below N=3 there are no positive three-part compositions.

value.rationale: For two common disproportionality measures the exact threshold identifies when rankings can disagree, explaining the tradeoff between total and concentrated error. The integer cutoff is a reproducible minimal test of that effect under explicit positivity and common granularity, rather than an arbitrary enumeration of election outcomes. It is not a claim about actual electorate sizes or electoral-system quality.
